transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Thank you for seeing me, Doctor. Lately, my mind just feels so foggy and I can’t seem to focus or make decisions the way I used to. It’s been incredibly frustrating because it's starting to get in the way of my everyday life.
Have you noticed any problems with your memory, like forgetting things you did recently or repeating questions?
I haven't really noticed repeating questions or forgetting things I just did. It's more that my mind feels extremely foggy, and it is just so hard to focus or make decisions lately.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for the past two weeks?

Yes, I have. Most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, like someone drained all the color out of my life, and it just hangs over me. This low period has actually been dragging on for about six months now.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy, even things that once made you happy?

Yes, I really have. I used to get so much joy out of sketching store layouts and making pottery for my online shop, but now I just stare at the plans or the clay and feel completely empty. I usually end up just turning off the light and going back to bed or watching TV.
Have you also noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels, and do you feel unusually guilty or worthless most days?

No matter how much I sleep, I feel completely wrung out and exhausted, like I've already worked a full shift before I even have my coffee. I also constantly beat myself up and feel terrible, like I'm letting my sister and my clients down because I can't keep up. I haven't really noticed much of a change in my appetite, though.
How long have you been experiencing this low mood, loss of interest, and other symptoms like fatigue and feelings of worthlessness?
This current low period has been dragging on for about six months now. It really started a few weeks after I began making regular weekend trips to help my sister with her heart condition.

There is no indication of manic or hypomanic symptoms, ruling out bipolar disorder. No significant change in appetite or sleep disturbance was noted, but the core psychological and somatic symptoms are present. No features suggesting schizophrenia, delusional disorder, or adjustment disorder with prolonged duration make other diagnoses less likely. The onset following a psychosocial stressor (caring for sister) supports a depressive episode in a vulnerable individual. Thus, F32 remains the primary candidate.
